description:
Programme or Project Overview

Karolinska Institutet advertises a post-doctoral researcher position in molecular eicosanoid research, funded as a scholarship. Eicosanoids are lipid mediators derived from polyunsaturated fatty acids that regulate inflammation, immunity and tissue repair, and alterations in eicosanoid networks are implicated in inflammatory disease, pain and cancer. The postdoctoral researcher will study eicosanoid formation and signalling with lipidomics, enzymology and cell-based models, contributing to the group's translational research agenda.

Karolinska Institutet is Sweden's premier medical university and hosts one of Europe's densest biomedical research environments. The scholarship-funded position provides a stipend per KI's scholarship terms for a fixed period, dedicated laboratory space and access to the institute's core facilities, including advanced lipidomics platforms. The post suits an early-career researcher aiming to specialise in lipid mediator biology and inflammatory mechanisms.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a PhD in biochemistry, molecular biology, pharmacology, immunology or a closely related discipline, with experience in lipid biochemistry, mass spectrometry or inflammation models being an advantage. Applications are submitted through Karolinska Institutet's Varbi portal with a CV, publication list, references and a letter of motivation, and the closing date for applications is 5 November 2026.

Highlights

  • Postdoctoral scholarship position in molecular eicosanoid research
  • Lipid mediators in inflammation, immunity and repair
  • Lipidomics and enzymology approaches
  • Karolinska Institutet biomedical research environment
  • Core-facility access including lipidomics platforms
  • Closing date: 5 November 2026
